title: Cryptography
tagline: Perfect secrecy, computational security, block ciphers, hash functions and MACs, number theory, public-key encryption, digital signatures, protocols and post-quantum cryptography
summary: Modern cryptography turns secrecy and authenticity into precise definitions with provable guarantees. This course develops symmetric encryption, block ciphers and modes of operation, hash functions and message authentication, the number theory behind public-key cryptography, key exchange, public-key encryption and digital signatures, secure protocols such as TLS, and the post-quantum schemes now being deployed.

chapters.title: Classical ciphers and perfect secrecy
chapters.summary: Historical ciphers and how they were broken, Shannon’s perfect secrecy and the one-time pad.

chapters.title: Computational security and pseudorandomness
chapters.summary: Security definitions and negligible advantage, pseudorandom generators and pseudorandom functions.

chapters.title: Block ciphers and modes of operation
chapters.summary: The design of AES, security against chosen-plaintext attacks, and modes such as CBC and CTR.

chapters.title: Hash functions and message authentication
chapters.summary: Collision resistance, SHA-2 and SHA-3, MACs and HMAC, and authenticated encryption.

chapters.title: Number theory for cryptography
chapters.summary: Modular arithmetic and groups, fast exponentiation, primality testing, and the factoring and discrete-logarithm problems.

chapters.title: Key exchange and public-key encryption
chapters.summary: Diffie–Hellman over finite fields and elliptic curves, RSA and ElGamal encryption, and chosen-ciphertext security.

chapters.title: Digital signatures and certificates
chapters.summary: RSA and elliptic-curve signatures, hash-and-sign, certificates and public-key infrastructure.

chapters.title: Cryptographic protocols
chapters.summary: Authenticated key exchange and TLS 1.3, secret sharing and zero-knowledge proofs.

chapters.title: Post-quantum cryptography
chapters.summary: Quantum threats to public-key cryptography, lattice-based and hash-based schemes, and the move to new standards.
